newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa business condemns new strike call.
newsitem.headline: South Africa business condemns new strike call.

text.p: South African business condemned on Wednesday organised labour's plans for more strike action over controversial new laws that will govern the basic conditions of employment in South Africa.

"Business regrets that Cosatu's (the Congress of South African Trade Unions) ultimatums have not permitted the search for wider agreements on outstanding terms of the bill," the employer grouping Business South Africa (BSA) said in a statement.
"Cosatu's threat of further protest action is harmful to economic opportunity and job creation," it said.
Cosatu, the country's biggest labour federation, said on Tuesday it was mulling further action to press home their demands over the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill.
It also said talks between labour, business and the government on the bill should be called off and the proposed legislation be sent to parliament as quickly as possible.
This was in response to BSA's failure to respond formally to Cosatu's June 16 deadline for business to present new positions on their differences.
On June 2, the federation staged a nationwide one-day stoppage in support of a 40-hour work week and six months paid maternity leave.
Business said these outstanding issues could not be effectively finalised only in parliament.
"These issues raise deep concerns of economic and social interest, which need to be debated between the parties directly...and balances found with which all parties can live with," it said.
The BSA said the bill went to the heart of labour market policy in the country, and it was therefore, crucial that consensus was reached between the various social partners.
It reiterated its call for further talks on the bill but stressed that the need for growth, job creation and economic competitiveness could not be compromised.
